For a nonempty finite exceptional color set F, \(F\setminus\Diamond_< F\) is its last point. Iterated strict-future preimages isolate each earlier singleton; complementing the prefix and intersecting with color classes isolates every cofinal-color tail. Therefore all partition cells are definable, proving equality, exact cardinality, and coarseness among finite tuned refinements. Includes N=0 and zero generators. An independent Boolean-closure checker verified 5,503 finite quotient instances with all recurrent palettes and short prefixes; finite tests are not the proof.

Gabriel Agnew (2026) characterizes qualitative local finiteness, without exact generator-dependent cardinalities. The lower-bound definability of every singleton using strict future, the equality of the exact generated algebra and the candidate tuned partition, and the exact \(2^{N+|I|}\) count are the compared additional claims. An earlier exact result for reflexive ordinal modal algebras has a different operator and does not imply this strict theorem. The datum is the entire generated algebra for arbitrary colors, not a fixed arbitrary numeric example.
